title: Phones, apps & payments
goal: Pay by UPI, sort out a failed payment, order things online, fix the WiFi, spot a scam and talk about posts and reels — the way people in Mumbai and Pune actually do.
intro:
In Maharashtra today the vegetable seller, the auto driver and the tapri all have a QR code, and **जीपे कर** 'GPay me' is a normal sentence. Tech Marathi is mostly English words — **पेमेंट**, **ऑर्डर**, **रिस्टार्ट**, **रील** — held together by Marathi grammar.

That grammar is what this unit is about. First, how a loanword becomes a verb with **करणे** (someone does it: **मी पेमेंट केलं**) or **होणे** (it happens: **पेमेंट झालं**), and why the gender of the English word suddenly matters (**ऑर्डर केली**, but **पेमेंट केलं**). Second, real-life conditions the way people say them: **पेमेंट फेल झालं तर?** 'what if the payment fails?', **बटण दाबलं की…** 'press the button and…', and the formal **-ल्यास** you'll read in every bank message.

grammar.title: English word + करणे or होणे: पेमेंट केलं, पेमेंट झालं
grammar.body:
Tech Marathi works like this: take an English word (usually a noun or a bare verb) and put a Marathi verb after it. The Marathi verb does all the grammar.

**करणे — when someone does it (transitive):** डाउनलोड **कर**, कोड स्कॅन **करा**, पैसे ट्रान्सफर **करतो**, लॉग इन **करता येत नाहीये**.
**होणे — when it happens by itself (intransitive):** ॲप डाउनलोड **होतंय** 'the app is downloading', पेमेंट **झालं** 'the payment went through', फोन हँग **झाला** 'the phone froze'. This is the same pairing as ठरवणे / ठरणे in Unit 31. Some loans only ever take होणे because nobody 'does' them: हँग, फेल, डाउन, कट.

Other helpers you'll hear: **टाकणे** 'put' for posting — फोटो **टाक**, स्टोरी **टाकली**; **मारणे** in Mumbai slang — कॉल **मार** 'give me a call'; and the brand name itself as a noun: **जीपे कर**, **फोनपे करतो**. And keep the good native verbs: **मागवणे** 'order in', **दाबणे** 'press', **चालणे** 'work'.

**The gender trap.** In the past tense, करणे goes into the ergative (Unit 16) and agrees with the object — so you need to know the **gender of the English word**:
- neuter: पेमेंट, ॲप, अकाउंट, नेट, वायफाय → मी पेमेंट **केलं**
- feminine: ऑर्डर, डिलिव्हरी, पोस्ट, रील, लिंक, कॅश, ऑफर → मी ऑर्डर **केली**
- masculine: पासवर्ड, पिन, मेसेज, फोन, क्यूआर कोड → मी पासवर्ड **बदलला**
With होणे it agrees with the subject the same way: फोन हँग **झाला** (m), पेमेंट **झालं** (n), ऑर्डर **आली** (f). When there's no real object (I downloaded, I logged in), use the neuter: मी डाउनलोड **केलं**.

grammar.title: Real conditions in everyday speech: -लं तर, -लं की, -ल्यास
grammar.body:
Unit 19 taught **जर … तर …** 'if … then …'. In everyday speech Marathi usually drops **जर** and builds the condition from the **past form** of the verb — even when talking about the future:

**past form + तर — 'if'**
पेमेंट फेल **झालं तर** काय करायचं? 'what do we do if the payment fails?'. ऑर्डर आज **आली तर** बरं होईल 'it'll be great if the order comes today'. This past form doesn't mean the past, just as English 'if it fails' doesn't mean the present. With **असणे** use its future instead: नेट **नसेल तर** 'if there's no internet', वायफाय **असेल तर** 'if there's WiFi'. Negative: ओटीपी **आला नाही तर** 'if the OTP doesn't come'.

**past form + की — 'whenever / as soon as'**
For things that always happen: हे बटण **दाबलं की** ॲप उघडतं 'press this button and the app opens', नेट **गेलं की** सगळं बंद होतं 'whenever the net goes, everything stops'.

**-ल्यास — 'in case of' (formal)**
The -ल्या form + **स**: पेमेंट फेल **झाल्यास** 'should the payment fail', पिन तीनदा **चुकल्यास** 'if the PIN is entered wrongly three times'. This is the language of bank SMSes, app screens and instructions.

**नाहीतर — 'otherwise, or else'**: लवकर ऑर्डर कर, नाहीतर ऑफर संपेल.

**The trap:** don't put the future before तर (~~फेल होईल तर~~). The condition takes the past form; the **result** takes the future or a command: फेल झालं तर मी कॅश **देईन**.

culture:
UPI has changed how Maharashtra pays. The vegetable seller, the auto driver, the tapri and the temple donation box all have a QR code, and many small shops have a little speaker that announces each payment out loud. The app names are verbs: **जीपे कर**, **फोनपे करतो**, **पेटीएम करा**. Cash is still accepted almost everywhere, and **कॅश ऑन डिलिव्हरी** is popular for online orders. In Mumbai and Pune, groceries arrive in ten minutes from quick-commerce apps, and food comes from Swiggy and Zomato. People say **मागवूया** for 'let's order in'.

Marathi does have official words for all this — **भ्रमणध्वनी** 'mobile phone', **संकेतस्थळ** 'website', **संगणक** 'computer' — and you'll see them in government notices and newspapers. Nobody says them out loud, though: in conversation it's फोन, वेबसाईट and लॅपटॉप, with Marathi verbs attached.

Marathi has a lively life online: Marathi **रील्स**, stand-up and memes, Marathi film songs trending on Instagram, and family WhatsApp groups full of **फॉरवर्ड**s and good-morning images. Scams are common too. The classic one is a message saying your **केवायसी** (KYC) has expired or your electricity will be cut tonight, with a link or a number to call. The rule everyone repeats: **बँक कधीच ओटीपी मागत नाही** 'the bank never asks for your OTP'.

tip.title: English word + करणे / होणे
tip.body:
- Someone does it: loan + **करणे**: स्कॅन **करा**, पैसे ट्रान्सफर **करतो**.
- It happens: loan + **होणे**: पेमेंट **झालं**, पैसे ट्रान्सफर **झाले**.
- In the past, केलं/झालं agrees with the English word's gender: पेमेंट (n) **केलं**, ऑर्डर (f) **केली**.
- The app name can be the verb: **जीपे कर**.

lessons.title: When a payment goes wrong

tip.title: If: -लं तर, -लं की, -ल्यास
tip.body:
- 'If' in speech: past form + **तर**: पेमेंट फेल **झालं तर** काय? (no जर needed). With असणे: नेट **नसेल तर**.
- 'Whenever': past form + **की**: बटण **दाबलं की** ॲप उघडतं.
- Formal 'in case': **-ल्यास**: फेल **झाल्यास**.
- Never फेल होईल तर — the future goes in the result.

tip.title: Try it: करून बघ
tip.body:
- 'Try doing' = stem + **ऊन बघ**: रिस्टार्ट **करून बघ**, वायफाय बंद **करून बघ**. Polite: **करून बघा**.
- 'It's not working': **चालत नाहीये**; it froze: **हँग झाला**.
- 'The net's gone': **नेट गेलं**; it's back: **नेट आलं**.

sentences.roman: ālaṃ neṭ! ātā tsāltaṃy.
sentences.en: The net's back! It's working now.

sentences.native: ॲप उघडून बघ, पेमेंट झालं असेल.
sentences.roman: æp ughḍūn bagh, pemeṇṭ dzhālaṃ asel.
sentences.en: Open the app and check — the payment has probably gone through.

sentences.native: वायफायचा पासवर्ड पाठवशील का?
sentences.roman: vāyfāytsā pāsvarḍ pāṭhavshīl kā?
sentences.en: Could you send me the WiFi password?

sentences.native: हे ॲप डाउनलोड कर, खूप भारी आहे.
sentences.roman: he æp ḍāunloḍ kar, khūp bhārī āhe.
sentences.en: Download this app, it's brilliant.

sentences.native: मला लॉग इन करता येत नाहीये, पासवर्ड विसरलो.
sentences.roman: malā lôg in kartā yet nāhīye, pāsvarḍ visarlo.
sentences.en: I can't log in, I've forgotten my password. (man)

sentences.native: तुझं इन्स्टावर अकाउंट आहे का?
sentences.roman: tudzhaṃ insṭāvar akāuṇṭ āhe kā?
sentences.en: Are you on Insta?

sentences.native: तिने कालच्या ट्रिपचे फोटो पोस्ट केले.
sentences.roman: tine kālchyā ṭripche phoṭo posṭ kele.
sentences.en: She posted the photos from yesterday's trip.

sentences.native: त्या रीलला दहा लाख लाईक्स आले!
sentences.roman: tyā rīllā dahā lākh lāīks āle!
sentences.en: That reel got a million likes!

sentences.native: मी तुला एक रील पाठवलीय, बघ!
sentences.roman: mī tulā ek rīl pāṭhavlīy, bagh!
sentences.en: I've sent you a reel, watch it!

sentences.native: ही पोस्ट सगळ्यांना शेअर कर.
sentences.roman: hī posṭ sagḷyānnā shear kar.
sentences.en: Share this post with everyone.

sentences.native: तो मला फॉलो करतो, पण मी त्याला नाही.
sentences.roman: to malā fôlo karto, paṇ mī tyālā nāhī.
sentences.en: He follows me, but I don't follow him.

sentences.native: आई फेसबुकवर सगळं फॉरवर्ड करते!
sentences.roman: āī fesbukvar sagḷaṃ fôrvarḍ karte!
sentences.en: Mum forwards everything on Facebook!

sentences.native: मराठी रील्स बघून मी खूप मराठी शिकलो!
sentences.roman: marāṭhī rīls baghūn mī khūp marāṭhī shiklo!
sentences.en: I've learned loads of Marathi from watching Marathi reels! (man)
